name: Alliance Relations
summary: Thrall seeks a careful hand to preserve peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to find Keldran near the western exit. The work calls for quiet diplomacy and intelligence to protect Thrall’s fragile peace.

sections.title: A Diplomatic Dilemma
sections.body: Thrall knows war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions with patience for a subtler path, one that looks beyond raw force.

sections.title: Keldran's Hovel
sections.body: Near Orgrimmar’s western exit, Keldran keeps a humble dwelling. He practices magic and covert arts, working with appearances, perception, and statecraft. Keldran seeks discreet operatives to serve the Warchief as the Horde faces a tense standoff with its bitter rivals.

faq.q: Who gives the quest Alliance Relations?
faq.answer: Craven Drok offers this work in Orgrimmar to Horde adventurers who have reached their thirtieth season of experience.
Keldran lives in a small hovel near Orgrimmar’s western exit, away from the city center.

faq.q: What is Keldran's role in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Keldran studies magic and mystical arts, assisting Warchief Thrall with discreet matters of diplomacy, intelligence, and the Horde’s public image.

faq.q: Why does Thrall care about diplomacy with the Alliance?
faq.answer: Raised among humans, Thrall understands their politics and military power. He knows outright war could destroy his young people, so he relies on prudence and measured statecraft to protect the Horde’s future.

faq.q: Does this quest lead to further missions?
faq.answer: Yes. Bringing this matter to Keldran begins a deeper discussion of the Horde’s standing with other factions and leads to further work in regional diplomacy and espionage.

faq.q: Why is discretion so important for this task?
faq.answer: Open conflict with the Alliance risks heavy casualties and could destabilize Kalimdor. Thrall relies on subtle operatives to address sensitive diplomatic friction before it erupts into war.

angles.text: For the Horde, this work shows the divide between traditional brute strength and Thrall’s more measured, diplomatic statecraft.
As an orc, you may know the axe as a way to settle conflict. Keldran’s approach calls for patience and tactical subtlety.
As a rogue, your skill with secrecy and perception suits Keldran’s work.
